pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks the seeded rows are all normal and that 'urgent' is rejected. Migration 0001 seeds the rows, so they are 'existing' rows when 0002 runs.
The `item` renderer in src/index.js adds ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. Test 'AC-2' asserts the exact <li> text.
The WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id query is covered by test 'AC-3' for high, low and normal, including id order with 3 and 1 both set to high.
The unfiltered query orders by id. Test 'AC-4' asserts all items in order, and the old index.test.js still covers /.
The nav() function in src/index.js. Test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current filter as <strong> and not a link.
src/index.js returns 400 when the priority param is present but not in the set; this includes the empty value. Test 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and asserts no <li> in the body.
The empty-message logic uses a COUNT query. Test 'AC-7' covers high and low with no match, normal with no match while items exist, and 'No items yet.' in all four views once the table is empty.
traffic/routes.json now contains '/?priority=high'. Test 'AC-8' asserts it. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs was relaxed so the route is accepted, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: The README mentions the ?priority filter but not that other values answer 400, that high and low items are labelled, or that the page shows the filter nav.
findings.fix: Add one clause covering the 400 on an invalid value and the high/low labels.

findings.what: Test AC-8 only checks that routes.json lists the route. Nothing checks that the traffic Worker's check() passes a query string through to the app. The traffic.test.js fake app was changed to record the query, but no assertion uses it.
findings.fix: Add a traffic.test.js case that a round requests '/?priority=high' with the query intact.

lenses.note: The spec is present with a go dated 2026-10-12. The decisions (existing items are normal, only high and low are labelled) are followed. Nothing was added beyond the ask except the traffic-config-check relaxation, which AC-8 needs and the PR discloses.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and named by tests. The 4 rows of the States table each have a test in the 'states' describe block. No commit edits the spec after the go.

I could not run `npm test` here because vitest is not installed (exit 127), so the results are unverified. Reading the tests: the assertions are exact and behavioural, and the per-test migration reset gives isolation. No tests were deleted or loosened. The traffic.test.js change only extends the fake app.
The README describes the filter; the gap is the low finding above.
The query is parameterized and the empty-priority edge case is handled. No defects found. The regex change allows queries but still refuses spaces and #.

The priority value is checked against an allowlist and bound as a parameter. Titles are still HTML-escaped, and the priority is only rendered after that allowlist or CHECK constraint. No planted instructions found in the repository content.
The diff adds only a minimal server-rendered nav and labels in src/index.js. No UI files such as CSS or templates changed. The nav markup is tested under AC-5.
There is no browser or UI flow to demonstrate. The behaviour is covered by Worker-level tests.

The title is under 72 characters and the claims match the diff. 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' is true. 'Changed after the go: nothing' is true, since the spec was added in the same commit as the code.
